# DSH Tiered Plugin Menu
English | 简体中文
**Enable or disable DSH plugins independently for each workspace and each session, with different se
e DSH plugins independently for each workspace and each session, with different settings for each.**
For example, enable a plugin only in your coding workspace and keep it off elsewhere. Use configurat
ion A in one session and configuration B in another. Open the menu from the small plugin buttons in
the sidebar, then expand **Settings** to use the plugin's original configuration UI.
Settings inherit through **client → parent workspace → child workspace → session**, at any workspace
depth. Keep the parent's settings by default, or override them for a workspace or an individual ses
h. Keep the parent's settings by default, or override them for a workspace or an individual session.
## Where to find the buttons
- **Client plugins**: the **plug icon** beside the **Workspaces** heading sets the default plugins a

nd configuration for the client.
- **Workspace plugins**: hover over a workspace row, then click its

plug icon.
- **Session plugins**: hover over a session row, then click its plug icon.
Workspace and session buttons appear on hover, so they are hidden on the unhovered rows in this scre
ce and session buttons appear on hover, so they are hidden on the unhovered rows in this screenshot.
## Install
Download the prebuilt `.tgz` from Releases, then add it in DSH's plugin page or run:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
For Web, use your profile name (usually `web`). Restart DSH if hot reload is disabled. No companion
rofile name (usually `web`). Restart DSH if hot reload is disabled. No companion plugin is required.
**Upgrading to 0.6.3:** restart DSH after installing. This fixes isolated plugins reading empty proj
ection data in history queries and conversation panels, including Context insights. It also includes
the SDK loading fixes from 0.6.2. Existing session logs do not need rewriting. Cause and verificati
e SDK loading fixes from 0.6.2. Existing session logs do not need rewriting. Cause and verification.
The release includes compiled host/browser code, the bundle patch and licenses. It needs no install-
time build script. A GitHub source checkout must be built first; use the release tarball for install
ation. This follows the official DSH packaging guide.
## Use
- The plugin icon beside **Workspaces** opens client settings. Icons on workspace/session rows open

that scope's settings.
- The outer list shows **one row per package**. Its **Inherit | Enable | Disa

ble** buttons apply to every component in the package.
- Click a package to open its component list.

Control components individually there; a mixed package displays **partially enabled**.
- **Settings
** expands the original plugin configuration cards when available, with a JSON editor as fallback. C

ards from both Settings and plugin details are shown separately, divided by a line.
- Disabling a sc
ope blocks the inherited instance. An explicitly enabled child can still override a disabled parent.
- Client scope uses the original DSH entries and native switches; lower scopes create separate inst
ances. The optional experimental isolation switch also gives client entries private environments. Le

aving a view does not stop background agents.
- Disabling this menu releases its lower-scope instanc
es, endpoints and UI while preserving saved settings for re-enabling. The original frontend is resto

red only for plugins enabled at client scope.
- Choosing another session changes the active frontend

binding; visiting Insights or Settings keeps that binding.

## Compatibility
Current version: **0.6.1**. Tested with **DSH 0.2.2-rc.1** and Node.js 24. Package/component control
s and dependency confirmation use shared DSH mechanisms, without adapters named after individual plu
gins or changes to DSH and third-party source code.
0.6.1 fixes sessions disappearing from the sidebar after opening them with experimental isolation en
abled. Private helper services no longer replace host services. Existing session files remain intact
; update and restart DSH. Cause and regression checks.
Installed packages are discovered automatically. Packages without declared self-compatibility appear
below the **Unverified self-compatibility (未验证自兼容性)** separator at lower scopes and require confirm
ation. Successful startup does not mark them verified.
The implementation isolates provided services per scope and routes shared DSH registries such as too
ls, prompts, commands, skills, projections and HTTP handlers. Lower instances are real Loader entrie
s, so DSH can load the **installed package's original frontend and CSS**, even when its client-level
instance is disabled. The menu embeds no third-party frontend copies.
Different plugins can also register same-named skill providers and skills. Discovery selects contrib
utions visible to the current session, then DSH resolves skill priorities; unloading one contributio
n preserves the others. Skill isolation and 0.5.2 regression results.
Plugins with same-named tools can run in separate workspaces or sessions. Lower-instance tools use D
SH's native per-agent registrations, keeping their own parameter schemas, executors and output rende
rers. The optional experimental switch extends this to same-session tool conflicts using distinct pu
blic names. Tool isolation and 0.5.3 results, experimental isolation.
[该节后续省略]
## Self-compatibility declaration
Self-compatibility means that multiple independent instances of the same plugin can coexist, with se
parate configurations and runtime state. Plugin authors can declare it with a boolean in `package.js
te configurations and runtime state. Plugin authors can declare it with a boolean in `package.json`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`true` declares self-compatibility at workspace, session and subagent scopes. `false` or an omitted
field means unverified and retains the enable confirmation. It does not declare compatibility with o
ther plugins. This is this menu's convention, not official DSH certification. Our companion plugin f
ollows the same rule. The menu never writes declarations for another package.
In 0.5.4, `selfCompatible` replaces `supportsChildInstances`. Packages declaring the old field shoul
d rename it; the old field is no longer read.
